task.title: Defending a curriculum change
task.scenario: You are an education adviser presenting a proposed change to a school board that includes parents and teachers.
task.prompt: Imagine you are speaking to the board. Present the proposal, respond to critical questions and persuade the sceptical members.
instructions: Read what the other person says. Then write what you would say in reply to each line.
Use complete sentences, as you would in a real conversation.
In this version your answer is typed. Pronunciation is not assessed.
task.main_question: Please explain why you recommend replacing some exams with project work.
follow_up_questions: Parents worry that projects are marked less fairly than exams. How would you address that?
Some teachers say they do not have time for this. What is your response?
If the pilot fails, what would you recommend?

content_points: Please explain why you recommend replacing some exams with project work.
Parents worry that projects are marked less fairly than exams. How would you address that?
Some teachers say they do not have time for this. What is your response?
If the pilot fails, what would you recommend?
required_elements: Respond to: Please explain why you recommend replacing some exams with project work.
Respond to: Parents worry that projects are marked less fairly than exams. How would you address that?
Respond to: Some teachers say they do not have time for this. What is your response?
Respond to: If the pilot fails, what would you recommend?
optional_elements: extra detail, examples or a personal anecdote
organisation: answer each question or cue point in turn, adding reasons and examples
expected_response.discourse_complexity: Fully organised extended discourse with explicit argument structure.
expected_response.linguistic_demand: Well-structured, detailed discourse on complex and abstract topics; qualified positions; flexible register; nominalisation and hedging.
expected_response.cognitive_demand: Persuade a defined audience; Adapt style and register to audience and purpose; Critically evaluate claims and evidence

examples.label: Illustrative outline only - not an answer key; many other responses are equally valid

learning_objectives.text: Present, defend and adapt an argument to sceptical listeners with tact and nuance

difficulty.language_demand: Well-structured, detailed discourse on complex and abstract topics; qualified positions; flexible register; nominalisation and hedging.
difficulty.cognitive_demand: Persuade a defined audience; Adapt style and register to audience and purpose; Critically evaluate claims and evidence
expected_performance: Responds fully, precisely and appropriately; anticipates implications; maintains the role and register.
Wide, precise vocabulary including idiomatic and less common items; fluent paraphrase.
Wide range used flexibly with majority of sentences error-free.
difficulty.rationale: Heuristic components (0=A1 .. 5=C2): {'grammar': 4.0, 'cognition': 4.0, 'length': 4.0, 'abstractness': 3.2, 'prompt_language': 1.18}; composite 3.64 -> C1. Original target C1. Computed from invited grammar, cognitive operations, expected length, abstractness and prompt language only.

criteria.name: Relevance and task fulfilment
criteria.description: Whether the response answers the question asked, covers the cue points or situation, and is appropriate to the role and audience.
criteria.successful_performance: Responds fully, precisely and appropriately; anticipates implications; maintains the role and register. Needs to respond to: Please explain why you recommend replacing some exams with project work. | Parents worry that projects are marked less fairly than exams. How would you address that? | Some teachers say they do not have time for this. What is your response? | If the pilot fails, what would you recommend?
criteria.weak_performance: Answers the surface of the question but not its implications.
criteria.expected_evidence: Each question or cue point addressed; relevance of content; fit with the situation. Check each question or cue point in turn.

criteria.name: Lexical resource
criteria.description: Range and precision of vocabulary used to talk about the topic.
criteria.successful_performance: Wide, precise vocabulary including idiomatic and less common items; fluent paraphrase.
criteria.expected_evidence: Topic vocabulary; variety; paraphrase; collocation. Expected vocabulary demands: assessment and curriculum; persuasion and diplomacy; evidence and fairness.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not penalise a correct plain word.

criteria.name: Grammatical range and accuracy
criteria.description: Range and accuracy of structures used; typed text may contain writing conventions the learner would not use in speech.
criteria.successful_performance: Wide range used flexibly with majority of sentences error-free.
criteria.expected_evidence: Structures used; error frequency and type. Structures invited by the task: hedging_and_tentative_language, mixed_conditionals, nominalisation, contrast_and_concession.
common_error_patterns: articles and prepositions in complex phrases
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Do not penalise spelling or punctuation errors in the typed text; they do not describe spoken grammar.

criteria.name: Development of ideas
criteria.description: How far ideas are explained, justified and supported with reasons, examples or comparisons.
criteria.successful_performance: Develops ideas in depth; considers alternatives; qualifies claims; supports with specific examples.
criteria.weak_performance: Uneven development; limited weighing of alternatives.
criteria.evaluation_limitations: Judge development relative to the format (a Part 1-style answer is short by design).

criteria.name: Fluency and coherence
criteria.description: How smoothly and logically a response is organised and extended. In the text MVP only the coherence and organisation aspects can be observed; real-time fluency (speed, pauses, hesitation) cannot.
criteria.successful_performance: Develops topics coherently with flexible cohesion and natural discourse markers.
criteria.weak_performance: Occasional loss of direction; over-reliance on fillers or discourse markers.
criteria.expected_evidence: Length and completeness of responses; order of ideas; discourse markers; (typed text: no timing evidence).
criteria.evaluation_limitations: TEXT MVP: hesitation, speech rate, self-correction and filled pauses cannot be observed. Judge organisation only; never infer 'fluent speech' from typed text.

not_assessed_by_design.name: Pronunciation
not_assessed_by_design.reason: TEXT MVP: no pronunciation score may be assigned. Do not infer pronunciation from spelling. Reserved for the future audio pipeline.

the cue-card points in any order

target_level_attainment.1: partial: some target-level features, frequent breakdowns
target_level_attainment.2: mostly secure: target-level features present with some lapses

scale.note: Uncalibrated evaluator scale. Do not convert to an IELTS band without separate calibration.

evaluator_output_contract: criterion_scores (with CEFR-band estimate and target-level attainment per criterion)
evidence_quotes (exact spans from the learner response)
evaluation_blueprint.notes: The illustrative outline in expected_response.examples is NOT an answer key. Accept any response that fulfils the task.
text_mvp_limitations: Pronunciation, intonation, stress and rhythm cannot be assessed from typed text: do not assign a pronunciation score.
Fluency in the sense of speech rate, pauses and hesitation cannot be assessed; only organisation and coherence can.
Do not state or imply that this evaluation is a complete assessment of speaking.

policy.observed_error_vs_weakness: A diagnostic category is an OBSERVED error pattern when at least one instance is found in a response. It may be reported as an INFERRED learning weakness only after >= 3 instances in one response set of >= 100 words (or >= 2 responses) and when the error is not explained by task demands (for example a tense the task did not invite).

diagnostics.observed_vs_inferred: An error is OBSERVED when an instance appears in the response. It may be recorded as an INFERRED weakness only under the policy in diagnostics.policy (repeated instances, enough text, and not explained by task demands).
